In this React Native + Expo p5 learning app, there's a "reference" screen/modal with a search icon. The user wants the search icon to act as an input — i.e., tapping it should focus/activate a text input so the system keyboard appears immediately and the user can start typing.

Please search for:
1. The reference screen/modal. Search for files and components with "reference", "ref", "search" in the name under src/app and src/components. Likely something like "reference.tsx", "ReferenceScreen", "ReferenceModal", "ReferenceSearch".
2. The search UI — is there a magnifying-glass icon that toggles a search input? A search bar that's initially hidden? Report the exact file + line numbers of the search icon button and the text input it reveals.
3. How the icon and input are wired — useState for visibility? A TextInput ref with focus()? Show the relevant JSX and handlers.
4. The current behavior when the search icon is tapped (does it just setShowSearch(true)? Does it auto-focus the input?).

Report file paths + line numbers + code excerpts. Read only, no edits.
Let me search for the reference screen/modal.

27: const SYMBOL_PATTERN = new RegExp(

32: function highlightSyntax(code: string, colorScheme?: "light" | "dark"): { text: string; color: string }[] {
33:  const theme = getEditorTheme("p5-learn", colorScheme || "dark");
34:  const KEYWORD_RE = /\b(function|if|else|for|while|return|let|const|var|new|this|class)\b/g;
35:  const P5_RE = new RegExp(`\\b(${P5_FUNCTION_NAMES.join("|")})\\b(?=\\()`, "g");
36:  const NUMBER_RE = /\b\d+(\.\d+)?\b/g;
37:  const STRING_RE = /("[^"]*"|'[^']*'|`[^`]*`)/g;
38:  const COMMENT_RE = /(\/\/.*)/g;
39:  const OP_RE = /([{}[\]();,.]|=>|[-+*/%&|^!<>=]=?)/g;
40: 
41:  const allMatches: { index: number; text: string; color: string }[] = [];
42:  const patterns: [RegExp, string][] = [
43:  [COMMENT_RE, theme.comment],
44:  [STRING_RE, theme.string],
45:  [KEYWORD_RE, theme.keyword],
46:  [NUMBER_RE, theme.number],
47:  [P5_RE, theme.function],
48:  [OP_RE, theme.operator],
49:  ];
50:  for (const [re, color] of patterns) {
51:  re.lastIndex = 0;
52:  let match;
53:  while ((match = re.exec(code)) !== null) {
54:  allMatches.push({ index: match.index, text: match[0], color });
55:  }
56:  }
57:  allMatches.sort((a, b) => a.index - b.index);
58: 
59:  const tokens: { text: string; color: string }[] = [];
60:  let lastEnd = 0;
61:  for (const m of allMatches) {
62:  if (m.index < lastEnd) continue;
63:  if (m.index > lastEnd) {
64:  tokens.push({ text: code.slice(lastEnd, m.index), color: theme.fg });
65:  }
66:  tokens.push({ text: m.text, color: m.color });
67:  lastEnd = m.index + m.text.length;
68:  }
69:  if (lastEnd < code.length) {
70:  tokens.push({ text: code.slice(lastEnd), color: theme.fg });
71:  }
72:  return tokens.length > 0 ? tokens : [{ text: code, color: theme.fg }];
73: }

75: function parseDescription(
76:  text: string,
77:  onSymbolPress: (name: string) => void,
78:  colors: Record<string, string>,
79:  accentColor?: string,
80: ): React.ReactNode[] {
81:  if (!text) return [<Text key="empty" style={{ color: colors.textSecondary }} />];
82: 
83:  const parts: React.ReactNode[] = [];
84:  let lastIndex = 0;
85:  let match: RegExpExecArray | null;
86:  const seenSymbols = new Set<string>();
87: 
88:  SYMBOL_PATTERN.lastIndex = 0;
89: 
90:  while ((match = SYMBOL_PATTERN.exec(text)) !== null) {
91:  if (match.index > lastIndex) {
92:  parts.push(
93:  <Text key={`txt-${lastIndex}`} style={{ color: colors.textSecondary }}>
94:  {text.slice(lastIndex, match.index)}
95:  </Text>
96: );
97:  }
98:  const symbolName = match[0];
99:  const isFirst = !seenSymbols.has(symbolName);
100:  seenSymbols.add(symbolName);
101:  if (isFirst) {
102:  parts.push(
103:  <Text
104:  key={`sym-${match.index}`}
105:   style={{ color: accentColor || colors.textSecondary, fontWeight: "700", textDecorationLine: "underline" }}
106:  onPress={() => onSymbolPress(symbolName)}
107:  >
108:  {symbolName}
109:  </Text>
110: );
111:  } else {
112:  parts.push(
113:  <Text key={`sym-${match.index}`} style={{ color: colors.textSecondary }}>
114:  {symbolName}
115:  </Text>
116: );
117:  }
118:  lastIndex = match.index + match[0].length;
119:  }
120: 
121:  if (lastIndex < text.length) {
122:  parts.push(
123:  <Text key={`txt-${lastIndex}`} style={{ color: colors.textSecondary }}>
124:  {text.slice(lastIndex)}
125:  </Text>
126: );
127:  }
128: 
129:  return parts.length > 0 ? parts : [<Text key="full" style={{ color: colors.textSecondary }}>{text}</Text>];
130: }

I have everything needed. Here are the findings.

## Summary

The reference feature lives in two files:
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/app/ref/index.tsx` — the Reference screen (route `/ref`), which renders a floating "magnify" FAB and toggles a search overlay.
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx` — the modal overlay containing the actual `TextInput`.

There is no "hidden search bar" that appears inline; the magnifying-glass icon is a FAB that opens a `Modal` containing the input. The input does already auto-focus when the modal mounts, but only because of a static React prop — there is no imperative `inputRef.current?.focus()` tie-in.

## 1. The reference screen/modal + search components

- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/app/ref/index.tsx` — `Reference` component (default export) and its `SymbolDetail` sub-component. Route is `/ref` (with optional `?symbol=`).
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx` — `SearchOverlay` (default export). Rendered from `ref/index.tsx`.

## 2. Search icon button and the text input it reveals

### Search icon FAB (reference list view) — `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/app/ref/index.tsx:457-464`
```tsx
<Pressable
  onPress={() => setSearchVisible(true)}
  style={[styles.searchFab, { backgroundColor: derivedColors.primary }]}
  accessibilityRole="button"
  accessibilityLabel="Search symbols"
>
  <MaterialCommunityIcons name="magnify" size={24} color={colors.onPrimary} />
</Pressable>
```

### Second search icon FAB (symbol detail view) — `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/app/ref/index.tsx:346-353`
```tsx
<Pressable
  onPress={onOpenSearch}
  style={[styles.searchFab, { backgroundColor: derivedColors.primary }]}
  accessibilityRole="button"
  accessibilityLabel="Search symbols"
>
  <MaterialCommunityIcons name="magnify" size={24} color={colors.onPrimary} />
</Pressable>
```
(`onOpenSearch` is passed in from the parent at line 378 as `() => setSearchVisible(true)`.)

### The TextInput revealed by the icon — `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx:53-63`
```tsx
<TextInput
  ref={inputRef}
  value={query}
  onChangeText={setQuery}
  placeholder="Search symbols..."
  placeholderTextColor={colors.onSurfaceVariant}
  style={[styles.searchInput, { color: colors.onSurface }]}
  autoCapitalize="none"
  autoCorrect={false}
  autoFocus
/>
```
There is also a decorative magnify icon at `SearchOverlay.tsx:52` inside the search bar:
```tsx
<MaterialCommunityIcons name="magnify" size={18} color={colors.onSurfaceVariant} />
```

## 3. How the icon and input are wired

State lives in the `Reference` parent component, not in the overlay:

- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/app/ref/index.tsx:363` — `const [searchVisible, setSearchVisible] = useState(false);`

The overlay is mounted unconditionally and just receives `visible`:
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/app/ref/index.tsx:465-469` (list view)
  ```tsx
  <SearchOverlay
    visible={searchVisible}
    onClose={() => setSearchVisible(false)}
    onSelectSymbol={handleSelectSymbol}
  />
  ```
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/app/ref/index.tsx:379-383` (detail view, identical wiring)

Inside `SearchOverlay`:
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx:18` — `const [query, setQuery] = useState("");`
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx:19` — `const inputRef = useRef<TextInput>(null);`  ← declared but never used to call `.focus()`
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx:40-44` — `handleClose` clears the query, dismisses the keyboard, and calls `onClose()`:
  ```tsx
  const handleClose = useCallback(() => {
    setQuery("");
    Keyboard.dismiss();
    onClose();
  }, [onClose]);
  ```
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx:47` — `<Modal visible={visible} transparent animationType="fade" onRequestClose={handleClose}>`

So the visibility flow is purely declarative: parent's `setSearchVisible(true)` → `SearchOverlay`'s `visible` prop flips → React Native `Modal` mounts its children.

## 4. Current behavior when the search icon is tapped

Tapping the FAB only calls `setSearchVisible(true)` (lines 458 and 378). It does **not** imperatively focus the input.

Auto-focus today relies entirely on the `autoFocus` prop on `TextInput` (`SearchOverlay.tsx:62`). Because the `Modal` is always mounted (it is rendered unconditionally at `ref/index.tsx:465` and `:379`) and only its `visible` flag changes, `autoFocus` only fires on the very first mount of the component — not on subsequent openings. So when a user opens the search overlay a second time (after closing it), the input is **not** refocused, and the system keyboard will not appear automatically.

Note that `inputRef` is created (`SearchOverlay.tsx:19`) but never used — there is no `useEffect` reacting to `visible` that calls `inputRef.current?.focus()`. If you want the keyboard to appear reliably on every open, an effect like this is the missing piece:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  if (visible) inputRef.current?.focus();
}, [visible]);
```
(plus likely removing the static `autoFocus` prop, or guarding it).

Additional context: the same `setSearchVisible(true)` path is also reachable from the shake menu (`ref/index.tsx:394-397` and `:480-483`), so any focus fix in `SearchOverlay` would benefit both entry points.
